flawed_step: Step 1: A proof would need to establish that stability forces uniqueness, but this cannot be justified from the definition. Stability only excludes blocking pairs and permits multiple stable matchings.
counterexample: Let n=2. Men: m1 ranks w1>w2; m2 ranks w2>w1. Women: w1 ranks m2>m1; w2 ranks m1>m2. Both matchings {(m1,w1),(m2,w2)} and {(m1,w2),(m2,w1)} are stable.
assessment_summary: The first matching has no blocking pair because each man has his first choice. In the second, (m1,w1) is not blocking because w1 prefers m2, and (m2,w2) is not blocking because w2 prefers m1. Thus a strict, complete instance can have two stable matchings, so the statement is false.
